Sticker on top of console reads '9.0'.
PlayStation logo visible on top surface in photos 0, 1, and 2.

risks.risk: The firmware may be higher than 9.00, making the 'hacked' claim false.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen showing the software version.

risks.risk: The internal hard drive or optical disc drive may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video of a game loading from the hard drive and a disc being read.

risks.risk: The controller may have analog stick drift or button malfunctions.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being tested in a game or diagnostic app.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and navigating the home menu.
Photo of the System Information screen showing the firmware version.
Photo of the installed games library on the dashboard.
Video demonstrating the controller working without stick drift.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Sony PlayStation 4. It is priced at its worst case (not working and unhacked) because there is no proof of functionality and the seller makes an impossible claim regarding 'FIFA 26'.
